captions.text: Coere can score its own memory, right from the dashboard.
In Settings, Enable Dev Tools adds Benchmarks and Evals to the dashboard.
Runs use a separate scratch memory. Maya’s own chats and memory are never touched.
She downloads LoCoMo, a public benchmark of long conversations.
Before anything runs, it says about how much the run will cost.
Start builds a memory from the conversations, then answers each question and judges the answers.
The result scores it the benchmark’s own way, by category, and says what each part cost.
It also shows how little context Coere sent, against the whole history.
Export .txt saves the run as a plain report, with every case, its answer and its score.
A second run uses a cheaper judge. She ticks both runs and presses Compare.
Each score and cost side by side, with the change, ready to export.
Evals runs Coere’s own checks, the same cases as the command line. Check mode costs nothing.
Every check held. Each case shows what it expected and what it got.
Benchmarks and Evals stay off until Dev Tools is on.
